title: Turning recommendations into action: A post-evaluation psychological service model to support families in pediatric care.
abstract: Pediatric psychological evaluations generate recommendations intended to guide treatment, educational planning, and service access; however, health systems often lack structured mechanisms to support families in implementing these recommendations. This study utilized a retrospective, observational design to describe the naturalistic clinical workflow of a post-evaluation psychological service model. A structured follow-up program, designed to address barriers to follow-through and enhance continuity of care within a pediatric assessment setting, was implemented and staffed by supervised postdoctoral fellows. The service provided caregiver-focused follow-up visits tailored to referral questions from evaluating psychologists and family-identified needs. Medical records and referral forms were reviewed and coded for referral targets, family-reported barriers, and clinician-provided services. Between September 2023 and April 2025, a total of 154 families participated (patient age = 8.29 years,= 3.59), with common diagnoses including attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder, autism spectrum disorder, language disorders, and anxiety. Overall, families were referred for follow-up across diverse domains, most frequently troubleshooting service access (72%), educational programming (68%), current concerns (56%), and medication management (45%). Caregivers reported at least one barrier to recommendation implementation in 83% of cases, with the most common challenges involving access to behavioral/mental health services (52%) and educational supports (41%). Clinicians addressed multiple areas per family, most often providing guidance on educational programming (61%), symptom management (60%), assessment of current functioning (56%), and referral coordination (51%). These findings highlight substantial unmet service needs following pediatric psychological evaluation and demonstrate the feasibility of a structured follow-up psychological program embedded within a larger pediatric health care system. Integrating post-evaluation support into pediatric assessment programs may improve care coordination, reduce implementation barriers, enhance the practical utility of recommendations, and improve outcomes for children and families.
